dc:title: DFU HBOT Bounded Regimen and Execution Burden

A clinical practice guideline for the use of hyperbaric oxygen therapy in the treatment of diabetic foot ulcers. Undersea & Hyperbaric Medicine. 2015;42(3):205-247. UHMS DFU guideline.

Huang ET, Mansouri J, Murad MH, Joseph WS, Strauss MB, Tettelbach W, Worth ER. A clinical practice guideline for the use of hyperbaric oxygen therapy in the treatment of diabetic foot ulcers. Undersea & Hyperbaric Medicine. 2015;42(3):205-247. UHMS DFU guideline.

dc:description: This knowledge object estimates the execution burden of a contemplated outpatient HBOT course. It combines a fixed population-level regimen range with one selected facility, patient-reported travel distance and duration, and reported weekday-attendance difficulty.

schema:creator.schema:name: Knowledge Systems Lab
schema:creator.schema:affiliation: Knowledge Systems Lab, University of Michigan Medical School

koio:hasKnowledge.dc:title: Regimen Range
koio:hasKnowledge.dc:description: Return the governed Fixed Regimen Range Response containing the shorter and longer general scenarios
koio:hasKnowledge.dc:purpose: Regimen Range provides the fixed, general 30-40-session HBOT planning scenarios that are used to calculate patient burden without selecting or personalizing a regimen for the patient.

koio:hasEvidentialBasis.dc:bibliographicCitation: Löndahl M, Katzman P, Nilsson A, Hammarlund C. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy facilitates healing of chronic foot ulcers in patients with diabetes. Diabetes Care. 2010;33(5):998-1003. doi:10.2337/dc09-1754.
koio:hasEvidentialBasis.dc:description: HODFU trial treatment schedule supplies the longer general planning scenario: up to 40 sessions, five sessions per week over eight weeks. It does not select a regimen for an individual patient or establish the burden-analysis calculation.

koio:hasEvidentialBasis.dc:bibliographicCitation: Fedorko L, Bowen JM, Jones W, et al. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy does not reduce indications for amputation in patients with diabetes with nonhealing ulcers of the lower limb: a prospective, double-blind, randomized controlled clinical trial. Diabetes Care. 2016;39(3):392-399. doi:10.2337/dc15-2001.
koio:hasEvidentialBasis.dc:description: Fedorko trial treatment schedule supplies the shorter general planning scenario: 30 sessions, five sessions per week over six weeks. It does not select a regimen for an individual patient or establish the burden-analysis calculation.

schema:hasPart.dc:title: Regimen scenario implementation
schema:hasPart.dc:description: The shorter and longer general planning scenarios in showRegimenRange encode the 30- and 40-session anchors. This code passage is implementation, not additional clinical evidence.

koio:hasKnowledge.dc:title: Burden Questionnaire Logic
koio:hasKnowledge.dc:description: Burden Questionnaire Logic interactively collects and confirms the patient's selected treatment location, travel distance and time, and expected weekday-attendance difficulty.
koio:hasKnowledge.dc:purpose: Its purpose is to produce one confirmed, standardized patient response that can be used by Burden Response Analysis to calculate execution burden.

koio:hasEvidentialBasis.dc:bibliographicCitation: Undersea and Hyperbaric Medical Society. UHMS Accredited Hyperbaric Medicine Facilities. June 2025; list marked A/O 2025-06-30 on each page.
koio:hasEvidentialBasis.dc:description: Dated source for the facility choices represented in the KO's versioned U.S. provider-roster snapshot and collected by Burden Questionnaire Logic. It is not evidence of HBOT treatment effectiveness, current facility availability, or the burden-analysis calculation.

schema:hasPart.dc:title: Completed questionnaire response implementation
schema:hasPart.dc:description: The questionnaire implementation normalizes the selected facility and the three reported burden inputs into a completed response. The facility-list source supports the roster choices, not the patient's answers.

koio:hasKnowledge.dc:title: Burden Response Analysis
koio:hasKnowledge.dc:description: Burden Response Analysis computes the execution burden of a contemplated outpatient HBOT course by combining the fixed population-level regimen envelope with one selected facility, patient-reported travel, and reported weekday-attendance difficulty.
koio:hasKnowledge.dc:purpose: Its purpose is to produce a standardized execution burden response that can be used to inform patient and clinician decision-making.

schema:hasPart.dc:title: Execution burden level implementation
schema:hasPart.dc:description: The analysis combines a travel band with reported weekday-attendance difficulty to determine a five-level execution-burden category. No separate evidential basis is declared for this analysis element.

koio:hasService.dc:description: interactively collects the four required HBOT burden questionnaire inputs, generates the fixed regimen range artifact, runs the burden analysis, and prints all three spec-aligned JSON outputs.

koio:hasTest.dc:title: DFU HBOT Architecture Test
koio:hasTest.dc:description: This software behavior test file validates the package's end-to-end architecture by checking fixed regimen output, questionnaire completion, successful burden analysis behavior, and representative error paths for invalid request type and unresolved provider location.

koio:hasTest.dc:title: DFU HBOT Conformance Test
koio:hasTest.dc:description: This software schema test file verifies schema conformance across regimen-range requests/responses, completed questionnaire payloads, analysis request and completed result objects, and the ERR-07 error-result contract for missing required analysis input.

koio:hasTest.dc:title: Spec Conformance Fixture Audit Runner
koio:hasTest.dc:description: This script executes the full DFU HBOT conformance fixture bundle across regimen-range, questionnaire, provider-roster, burden-analysis, and audit/replay scenarios, then performs exact expected-vs-actual structural JSON comparisons and reports pass/fail (with strict nonzero exit on mismatch).
